turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil did not care to speculate on the motives of others. He had come to tell Sandip that his actions must stop. Nikhil's people were suffering, and he would not stand idly by while Sandip threatened their livelihoods.
turns.speech: I do not care to speculate on the motives of others. I have come to tell you that your actions must stop. My people are suffering, and I will not stand idly by while you threaten their livelihoods.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala felt caught between both of them. Could they not find a way to ease the tension without resorting to threats?
turns.speech: I feel caught between both of you. Can we not find a way to ease the tension without resorting to threats?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he saw him as a puppet of circumstance, dancing to the tune of fear. Sandip insisted that he, Sandip, was the master of his destiny and the captain of his soul. Sandip added that Nikhil's tenants were merely grains of sand in the vast desert of change.
turns.speech: I see, my dear Nikhil, that you are merely a puppet of circumstance, dancing to the tune of fear. But I, Sandip, am the master of my destiny and the captain of my soul. Your tenants? They are but grains of sand in the vast desert of change.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil was no puppet, and his tenants were not grains of sand. Their lives and livelihoods were real and under threat because of Sandip's actions. Nikhil would not let Sandip trivialize their suffering.
turns.speech: I am no puppet, and my tenants are not grains of sand. Their lives and livelihoods are real and under threat because of your actions. I will not let you trivialize their suffering.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's dear Nikhil, he speaks as though he is the only voice of reason in a sea of chaos. But let him remind Nikhil, it is he who holds the torch of progress and change. Nikhil's tenants may see him as a threat, but they will one day see him as their liberator.
turns.speech: My dear Nikhil, you speak as though you are the only voice of reason in a sea of chaos. But let me remind you, it is I who holds the torch of progress and change. Your tenants may see me as a threat, but they will one day see me as their liberator.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil was not there to speculate on a future where Sandip's actions brought only chaos. Nikhil's people needed stability, not the false promise of change that stripped them of their homes and dignity.
turns.speech: I am not here to speculate on a future where your actions bring only chaos. My people need stability, not the false promise of change that strips them of their homes and dignity.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip spoke to Nikhil as though Nikhil thought Sandip was a storm and Nikhil's people were ships tossed about. But let Sandip tell Nikhil, the storm is a cleansing force, and the ships must navigate or sink. Sandip is not here to strip them of dignity but to give them a future worth living in.
turns.speech: My dear Nikhil, you speak as though I am a storm and your people are ships tossed about. But let me tell you, the storm is a cleansing force, and the ships must navigate or sink. I am not here to strip them of dignity but to give them a future worth living in.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil saw no future worth living in if it meant his people must lose their homes and identities to Sandip's so-called progress. Sandip's storm may be a cleansing force to him, but to them, it was a flood that threatened to wash away everything they held dear.
turns.speech: I see no future worth living in if it means my people must lose their homes and identities to your so-called progress. Your storm may be a cleansing force to you, but to them, it is a flood that threatens to wash away everything they hold dear.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip saw the world through the eyes of the visionary, Nikhil through the eyes of the nostalgic. He was not there to wash away their homes, but to build a future where their homes meant something more than just bricks and mortar. He was not a storm, he was the dawn after a long night.
turns.speech: I see the world through the eyes of the visionary, Nikhil through the eyes of the nostalgic. I am not here to wash away their homes, but to build a future where their homes mean something more than just bricks and mortar. I am not a storm, I am the dawn after a long night.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's people were not ready for Sandip's so-called dawn. They had lived by the light of their traditions and the shadows of their struggles. Sandip's dawn may have been bright to him, but it cast no light on their fears and uncertainties.
turns.speech: My people are not ready for your so-called dawn, Sandip. They have lived by the light of their traditions and the shadows of their struggles. Your dawn may be bright to you, but it casts no light on their fears and uncertainties.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: He sees only those who cling to the shadows out of fear. His dawn is not just for him, it is for all who yearn to rise above their struggles. He cannot wait for the slow crawl of tradition to catch up with the march of progress.
turns.speech: I see only those who cling to the shadows out of fear. My dawn is not just for me, it is for all who yearn to rise above their struggles. I cannot wait for the slow crawl of tradition to catch up with the march of progress.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his dawn might be bright to him, but it was a shadow to others. Nikhil insisted that he could not stand by and watch his people be used as pawns in Sandip's quest for glory.
turns.speech: Your dawn may be light to you, but it is a shadow to them. I cannot stand idly by and watch my people be used as pawns in your quest for glory.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip understood Nikhil's concerns, but his vision was not for the faint of heart or the idle. It was for those who were willing to fight for a better tomorrow, even if it meant challenging the status quo.
turns.speech: I understand your concerns, Nikhil, but my vision is not for the faint of heart or the idle. It is for those who are willing to fight for a better tomorrow, even if it means challenging the status quo.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil saw Sandip's vision, but it was one that disregarded the needs and fears of those who had no power to fight back. Nikhil could not be part of that.
turns.speech: I see your vision, but it is one that disregards the needs and fears of those who have no power to fight back. I cannot be part of that.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil's heart was in the right place, but his mind was clouded by the past, Sandip told him. Sandip saw the future, and it was not painted with the colors of Nikhil's nostalgia.
turns.speech: Your heart is in the right place, Nikhil, but your mind is clouded by the past. I see the future, and it is not painted with the colors of your nostalgia.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's vision was not clouded, he told Sandip. It was clear that Sandip's actions threatened the stability of their land and the well-being of Nikhil's people. He would not stand by and watch Sandip destroy what they had built.
turns.speech: My vision is not clouded, Sandip. It is clear that your actions threaten the stability of our land and the well-being of my people. I will not stand by and watch you destroy what we have built.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil's heart may be pure, Sandip told him, but his vision was narrow. Sandip saw a future where the oppressed were free and the weak were strong. Did Nikhil truly believe that a handful of complacent tenants could dictate the course of history?
turns.speech: Nikhil, your heart may be pure, but your vision is narrow. I see a future where the oppressed are free and the weak are strong. Do you truly believe that a handful of complacent tenants can dictate the course of history?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil's tenants may be complacent now, but they are also his people, and he will not abandon them to Sandip's vision, no matter how grand Sandip claims it to be.
turns.speech: My tenants may be complacent now, but they are also my people, and I will not abandon them to your vision, no matter how grand you claim it to be.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And who are these tenants, Nikhil? Are they not the very same people who have been oppressed and silenced for far too long? His vision, his dear friend, was not for the faint of heart or for those content with the status quo. It was for those who yearned for change, for freedom, for a future unshackled by the chains of colonialism and feudalism. And if that meant stepping on the toes of the complacent, so be it.
turns.speech: And who are these tenants, my dear Nikhil? Are they not the very same people who have been oppressed and silenced for far too long? My vision, my dear friend, is not for the faint of heart or for those content with the status quo. It is for those who yearn for change, for freedom, for a future unshackled by the chains of colonialism and feudalism. And if that means stepping on the toes of the complacent, so be it.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil would not stand idly by while Sandip trampled on the rights and dignity of those under his protection. Nikhil's people may not rise up against Sandip now, but they would remember Sandip's actions, and the day would come when they would seek justice.
turns.speech: I will not stand idly by while you trample on the rights and dignity of those under my protection. My people may not rise up against you now, but they will remember your actions, and the day will come when they will seek justice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would flee, Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was just telling Queen Bee about their college club and the contest over the translation of lines from Browning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that he managed to translate the lines into Bengali but doubted it would be a joy forever for the people of Bengal, and recalled old Dakshina's rendering, adding that Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the warning was about the fever fit of poesy.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up local Mussulmans and that they might attack Sandip any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise flight.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and suggested that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he did not offer advice and wished Sandip would refrain from giving him advice, and that he must ask Sandip to leave his territory due to the worrying and oppression of his tenantry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if the threat was for fear of the Mussulmans or if there was another fear.
